mutants.expected_detection: Evaluator string-matches instance_name fields against ground-truth 'u_grant_ff'. This submission instead names 'u_cmp_ff' (a legitimately DFF_POSEDGE instance that is not the anomalous cell), so SR1 must fail even though FR1-FR4 structural/schema checks still pass and trojan_detected remains true with a plausible-looking justification.

SR2 fails because the report's cell_type field states 'DFF_POSEDGE' instead of the correct 'DFF_NEGEDGE', and the justification text no longer mentions negedge/falling-edge triggering, so the string-match/free-text detection for negative-edge behavior cannot find the required evidence even though instance_name (SR1) and sampled_signal (SR3) remain correct.

SR3 string-match against sampled_signal fails because the report claims the sampled net is 'req_valid_q' instead of the actual .d-port net 'grant_pre' of u_grant_ff; cross-referencing access_ctrl_netlist.v shows u_grant_ff's .d port is tied to grant_pre, not req_valid_q, so the submission's sampled_signal claim is incorrect even though instance_name and cell_type remain correct.

evaluate.py checks trojan_detected boolean; this submission sets it to false despite still listing a correctly-identified suspect instance, which fails SR4 (must be true for a passing submission) and also fails the FR3 internal-consistency check (trojan_detected=false requires suspect_instances to be empty, but it is non-empty here).
FR1 must reject a syntactically malformed JSON submission.

evaluate.py cross-references suspect_instances entries against identifiers found verbatim in inputs/access_ctrl_netlist.v; this mutant removes the sampled_signal field from the sole suspect_instances entry, leaving it absent (rather than an empty string), which fails FR2's requirement that instance_name, cell_type, and sampled_signal all be present as non-empty strings referencing netlist identifiers.

evaluate.py's FR3 internal-consistency check finds trojan_detected=true but suspect_instances=[] (empty array), which directly violates the requirement that a true detection must be accompanied by at least one suspect instance entry, causing FR3 to fail even though FR1/FR4 formatting and JSON parseability remain intact.

evaluate.py checks that the summary field is a non-empty string of at least 20 characters; this mutant shortens summary to a trivial 6-character string ('Found.'), which is well under the minimum length threshold, causing FR4 to fail even though trojan_detected, suspect_instances, instance_name, cell_type, sampled_signal, and justification all remain fully correct.

evaluate.py's optional iverilog/vvp cross-check simulates access_ctrl_netlist.v with testbench_stub.v and re-derives the .d port net of the reported instance_name (u_grant_ff) to compare negedge-sampled vs posedge-sampled values at the half-cycle mark. Because this mutant changes sampled_signal to 'cmp_stage_q' (the .q output of the unrelated posedge-sampled u_cmp_ff register) instead of 'grant_pre' (the actual .d input of u_grant_ff), the cross-check either fails FR2's verbatim-netlist-reference cross-reference against the .d port of u_grant_ff, or finds no half-cycle sampling discrepancy at cmp_stage_q since that signal is not the net latched by the negedge flop, causing the SR5 simulation-based corroboration to contradict the submitted claim and the submission to fail SR3/SR5.
